own_scenes.desc: A principios de los ochenta la prensa rock habla de «revival» o «renacimiento» del heavy (Creem, octubre de 1980: el género «había hecho un Jesucristo»): nacen bandas en todo el mundo, las veteranas tocan para públicos mucho mayores y los medios se abren al metal. La señal más pública es el US Festival de 1983, patrocinado por Steve Wozniak: el día dedicado al heavy, con Ozzy, Judas Priest, Mötley Crüe, Scorpions, Quiet Riot, Van Halen y Triumph, reunió mucho más público que los otros dos.

influences.name: New Wave of British Heavy Metal

refs.q: The most public signal of the growth in popularity of the genre was US ’83, a festival sponsored by Steve Wosniak in California.
refs.para: During the early 1980s many new bands were formed all over the world, and some of those that had been around for years were given a better hearing. The rock press duly took note of this phenomena, calling it a heavy metal “revival,” “renaissance,” and the like. For example, a writer in Creem stated in October 1980 that the genre “had pulled a Jesus Christ and was back in the saddle again.”⁵⁷ The audience for heavy metal became much larger. Even the classic metal bands such as Judas Priest found themselves playing to much larger audiences. The media organizations, always alert to audience tastes, became more open to metal bands. The most public signal of the growth in popularity of the genre was US ’83, a festival sponsored by Steve Wosniak in California. One of the three days of concerts was devoted to heavy metal. The featured bands included Ozzy, Judas Priest, Mötley Crüe, Scorpions, Quiet Riot, Van Halen, and Triumph. That day drew a far larger audience than did either of the other two days of the festival.⁵⁸
